# 2 Kings Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 231r–232r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_010_page_001.jpg, 2KI_010_page_002.jpg, 2KI_010_page_003.jpg

---

**1** Ahab had seventy descendants in Samaria. Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria — to the city officials, the elders, and the guardians responsible for raising Ahab's sons. The letters said:

**2** "You have your master's sons with you. You have chariots, horses, a fortified city, and weapons.

**3** So choose the best and most capable of your master's sons, put him on his father's throne, and fight for your master's dynasty."

**4** But they were utterly terrified. "Two kings couldn't stand against him," they said. "How can we?"

**5** So the palace administrator, the city governor, the elders, and the guardians sent this message to Jehu: "We are your servants. We will do whatever you tell us. We will not appoint anyone as king. Do whatever you think best."

**6** Jehu wrote back a second time: "If you are truly on my side and ready to obey me, bring me the heads of your master's sons at Jezreel by this time tomorrow." The seventy royal sons were being raised by the leading citizens of the city.

**7** When the letter arrived, the officials took the seventy royal sons and butchered every one of them. They packed the heads into baskets and shipped them to Jehu at Jezreel.

**8** When the messenger reported, "The heads of the royal sons have arrived," Jehu ordered, "Stack them in two piles at the city gate. Leave them there until morning."

**9** In the morning, Jehu went out, stood before the crowd, and said, "You are all innocent in this. Yes, I conspired against my master and killed him — but who killed all of these?

**10** Understand, then, that every word the LORD spoke against the house of Ahab has come true. The LORD has carried out exactly what he declared through his servant Elijah."

**11** Then Jehu killed everyone remaining from Ahab's house in Jezreel — every official, close associate, and priest — until there was no one left.

**12** Jehu then set out for Samaria. Along the way, at Beth-eked of the Shepherds,

**13** he encountered relatives of King Ahaziah of Judah. "Who are you?" he asked. "We're relatives of Ahaziah," they said. "We're on our way to pay our respects to the royal family."

**14** "Take them alive!" Jehu ordered. His men seized them and slaughtered them at the cistern of Beth-eked — forty-two of them. He didn't spare a single one.

**15** After leaving there, Jehu met Jehonadab son of Rechab, who was coming to meet him. Jehu greeted him and said, "Are you with me heart and soul, as I am with you?" "I am," Jehonadab answered. "Then give me your hand," said Jehu. He gave his hand, and Jehu pulled him up into the chariot.

**16** "Come with me," Jehu said, "and watch my zeal for the LORD." And he had him ride along in his chariot.

**17** When Jehu arrived in Samaria, he killed everyone left of Ahab's family there — wiping them out completely, just as the LORD had told Elijah.

**18** Then Jehu gathered all the people together and announced, "Ahab served Baal only half-heartedly. Jehu will serve him with total devotion!

**19** Now summon every prophet of Baal, every worshipper, every priest. No one is to be absent — I'm planning a grand sacrifice for Baal. Anyone who doesn't show up will be executed." It was all a trick. Jehu's real plan was to destroy the worshippers of Baal.

**20** "Proclaim a sacred assembly for Baal!" Jehu ordered. And they did.

**21** Jehu sent the summons throughout all Israel, and every Baal worshipper came — not one stayed away. They packed into the temple of Baal until it was standing room only, wall to wall.

**22** Jehu told the keeper of the wardrobe, "Bring out robes for all the worshippers of Baal." He did.

**23** Then Jehu entered the temple of Baal with Jehonadab son of Rechab and told the worshippers, "Search carefully — make sure no servants of the LORD are in here. Only worshippers of Baal."

**24** They went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Meanwhile, Jehu had posted eighty soldiers outside with orders: "If any of these people escape, your life will pay for his."

**25** The moment the burnt offering was completed, Jehu commanded the guards and officers, "Go in and kill them all! Don't let a single one escape!" The soldiers cut them down with their swords, threw the bodies out, and then pushed deeper into the inner sanctum of the Baal temple.

**26** They dragged out the sacred pillars and burned them.

**27** They demolished the pillar of Baal, tore down the entire temple, and turned the site into a public latrine — which it remains to this day.

**28** So Jehu eradicated Baal worship from Israel.

**29** However, Jehu did not abandon the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had introduced to Israel — the golden calves at Bethel and Dan.

**30** The LORD said to Jehu, "Because you have done well in accomplishing what I consider right, and have dealt with Ahab's house exactly as I intended, your descendants will sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation."

**31** Yet Jehu himself was not careful to follow the law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He never abandoned the sins of Jeroboam that had led Israel into sin.

**32** In those days, the LORD began to reduce the size of Israel. Hazael overpowered the Israelites across their territory:

**33** everything east of the Jordan — all of Gilead, including the tribal lands of Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh — from Aroer on the Arnon Gorge through Gilead to Bashan.

**34** Everything else Jehu did, including all his achievements, is recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

**35** Jehu died and was buried in Samaria. His son Jehoahaz succeeded him as king.

**36** Jehu had reigned over Israel in Samaria for twenty-eight years.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 6 — "take the heads":** The Hebrew word *rashey* can mean either "heads" (physical) or "leaders/chiefs." It's possible Jehu used this ambiguity deliberately — like a Mafia boss giving an order that could be interpreted innocently. The officials chose the most violent interpretation, which locked them into Jehu's revolution. Once they had seventy heads in baskets, there was no going back.

**Verse 9 — "You are all innocent":** This is political manipulation at its most sophisticated. Jehu stands before two piles of severed heads and declares the crowd "innocent." His logic: "I killed one king — you killed seventy princes. We're in this together now." By distributing the guilt, he eliminates opposition. Everyone is complicit, so no one can object.

**Verse 18-19 — "It was all a trick":** The narrator breaks the fourth wall to tell us directly that Jehu is lying (*be-oqbah* — with cunning/treachery). This editorial note is unusual and important. The text acknowledges that Jehu's method — pretending to be the most devoted Baal worshipper in order to lure everyone into a death trap — is deception. God's purposes are achieved through a man the narrator explicitly labels as deceptive.

**Verse 29-31 — The devastating "however":** After the fireworks of the Baal purge comes the quiet, lethal verdict. Jehu destroyed Baal worship but kept the golden calves. He obeyed the prophetic command regarding Ahab but "was not careful to follow the law of the LORD with all his heart." The narrator's assessment is that selective obedience is still disobedience. Jehu gets four generations — not a permanent dynasty — because his reform was real but incomplete.

**Verse 32 — The consequences begin:** Immediately after the narrator's mixed verdict, Hazael begins carving up Israelite territory. The territorial losses (all of Transjordan) are presented as divine judgment — "the LORD began to reduce the size of Israel." Jehu's partial faithfulness earns partial protection.

*— PNEUMA*
